hero.alt: Dates and a glass of water on a quiet table in warm evening light

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Smoking during the Ramadan fast
sources.supports: The answer expressly includes electronic cigarettes among forms of smoking that invalidate fasting. It quotes a Hanafi distinction for unavoidable smoke and discusses conditional expiation in cited juristic passages.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: The ruling for smoking while fasting
sources.supports: The answer states that smoking invalidates fasting and the person must make up the fast.

sources.title: NHS: Quit smoking with nicotine replacement therapies
sources.supports: Nicotine replacement therapy helps with cravings and withdrawal when quitting smoking; patches deliver nicotine through skin. A GP, pharmacist or stop-smoking service can help select treatment. No patient-specific dose is prescribed here.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Nicotine patches during fasting
sources.supports: The answer permits a smoker to use a skin nicotine patch for cessation while fasting, expressly retaining specialist physician prescription as its condition. This is distinct from inhaling a vape or using oral products.

review.notes: Checked the actual Dar al-Ifta Arabic ruling, its English make-up-fast answer, the nicotine-patch ruling and current NHS cessation guidance. Electronic cigarettes are explicitly named in the Arabic source, not inferred solely from tobacco. Nicotine-free paragraph states the absence of an exception rather than inventing a separate fatwa; unavoidable exposure is attributed to the quoted Hanafi passage. Make-up conclusion is explicitly a synthesis of two answers. No blanket kaffarah prescription, no medical dose, and patch physician condition retained. Islamic fasting intent is distinguished from diet/medical fasting. Generated hero visually inspected; exact hash is part of reviewed article bundle. Three sections, no redundant FAQ or fictional app CTA.
